Friday. Went to the tehsil office for my domicile certificate, which the scholarship form needs. The clerk, Chetan, glanced at my file and said, "This could take weeks. Or if a little extra reaches the peon, it could move today." My chest went tight. The scholarship closes next month.
I said I would think. On the bus I felt small and scared. Then I remembered the board at the entrance: the timelines and a grievance number. I had photographed it without thinking.
Tomorrow I will ask Chetan in writing for the stated time and an acknowledgement slip. If the file is still stuck, I will use the grievance number. Papa says to trust the process. I want to try.
Arohi

passage:
Last year my scholarship file sat at the district welfare office for two months. I'm Vishal, and I needed that money to pay my hostel fees.
On my fourth visit, the clerk leaned back and said, "Files like this move quicker if you add something, you know. Chai-paani." He smiled like it was a joke.
My stomach dropped. The fees were due in a week. For a moment I actually reached for my wallet.
Then I called my friend Ayesha, who's studying law. She said, "Don't. Check the scheme's official timeline online, write down the date and his words, and file a grievance on the portal. Keep screenshots."
I did all of it that night. I also wrote a polite letter to the district officer, with a copy for my records.
Nine days later, the money came. The clerk never looked at me again. I kept every screenshot, just in case.

qa.q: How long did Vishal's scholarship file sit at the office?
qa.a: It sat at the district welfare office for two months.

qa.q: What was Vishal feeling when he reached for his wallet?
qa.a: Vishal felt afraid and pressured, because the hostel fees were due in a week.

qa.q: What did Vishal do instead of paying, and why was it safer?
qa.a: Vishal checked the official timeline, recorded the clerk's words, filed a grievance on the portal and wrote to the district officer, which used official channels and kept proof.

qa.q: How might Ayesha have felt when Vishal called?
qa.a: Ayesha was probably concerned but steady, wanting her friend to avoid a bribe and use the proper process.

Student welfare officer's note, Tuesday.
Yusuf, 21, final-year student, came to me with his classmate Karthik. Yusuf's degree certificate had been "pending" at the university's records section for six weeks. His job offer in Pune requires it by the end of the month.
He said a staff member there told him, "It's a busy season. Some students help the process along." Yusuf understood this as a request for money. He looked frightened and said, "If I don't get it, I lose the job."
I told him he was right not to pay, and that we would use the official route. We wrote down exactly what was said, when and by whom. I emailed the registrar's office, copying the grievance cell, with his application number and deadline.
Next step: I will follow up tomorrow and, if needed, escalate to the Dean. Karthik offered to go with Yusuf to collect the certificate.

qa.q: How long had Yusuf's degree certificate been pending?
qa.a: It had been pending for six weeks.

qa.q: What was Yusuf afraid of?
qa.a: Yusuf was frightened that without the certificate he would lose his job offer in Pune.

qa.q: Why was the officer's approach a safer way forward?
qa.a: It used official procedures: recording what was said, emailing the registrar and grievance cell, and planning to escalate, instead of paying.

qa.q: How might Karthik feel about his friend's situation?
qa.a: Karthik seems supportive and concerned, coming along and offering to go with Yusuf to collect the certificate.

grounding: A note shows a young adult hinted to pay extra for his certificate, and a welfare officer helping him use records and complaint channels instead.

Friday
Went to the electricity office for the new meter for my tailoring corner. Third time. The lineman said, "Madam, these things take months. But if you're in a hurry, I can speak to someone." He rubbed his fingers together.
I felt sick and angry. I've saved for this shop for two years. I can't wait months. Part of me wanted to just pay and be done.
Then I remembered Sangeeta Aunty from the self-help group. She said, "Never pay. Ask for the receipt number, check the status online, and call the complaint line."
So I asked him for my application receipt number, politely. I wrote down his name. At home, Ma helped me register a complaint on the helpline, with the date.
It might still take time. But I'd rather wait honestly.
Vidya

qa.a: He rubbed his fingers together.

qa.a: She asked for her receipt number, wrote down the lineman's name, and registered a complaint on the helpline with her mother's help.

qa.a: Sangeeta Aunty would probably feel proud that Vidya followed her advice and chose the honest route.
